subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath and existing-ancestor caches inside plugin hook, plugin skill, and sandbox containment checks for this Windows performance fix?
rationale: The linked PR is narrower than the original process-wide global cache, but it still changes how security-sensitive path checks reuse filesystem answers within one operation.

options.title: Accept scoped caches after proof
options.body: Keep the linked PR direction, require fresh real-behavior proof on the final head, and land it once review clears the security-boundary risk.

options.title: Restrict caches away from containment checks
options.body: Reject cache reuse inside containment paths and pursue only non-security-boundary performance work.

options.title: Pause for a cache contract
options.body: Hold the linked PR until maintainers define the exact cache lifetime and invalidation contract for path-boundary helpers.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped caches after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR direction, require fresh real-behavior proof on the final head, and land it once review clears the security-boundary risk.
